goal: Review and finish the deployed Task 1 release without losing the already-running collector or falsifying its evidence.
preserve: The live collector remains outbound-only and keeps accumulating history while review runs.
USD, GBP and credits are not added; runway hours remain the only cross-provider ordering.
History stays keyed by stand world_epoch and fingerprint, and injected faults remain unknown rather than zero.
The real trace is redacted by substitution, never rewritten or shortened.
do_not_redo: Do not replace the collector architecture or restart the service unless a focused check proves the deployed process must change.
Do not discard the pre-existing api_stats change; the deployed VPS already runs it, so review and reconcile it with Git.
Do not invent a company-wide total across incompatible units.
review_decisions: Fix current-world scoping, complete-world admission, deploy atomicity, mutation-gate truthfulness, snapshot atomicity and bounded retry behavior before the next deploy.
Defer automatic sample deletion: retention would delete recorded evidence and requires an explicit user retention decision; current test-duration storage is not exhausted.

replan.reason: The user asked to continue the whole test after the focused Task 1 review, so the already-frozen Task 3 artifact branch is now part of this continuation.
preserve: Task 3 remains exactly one harness artifact with a three-line location and purpose note.
The artifact must be a real used workflow selected on measured evidence rather than a newly invented showcase.

verification.evidence: 12 of 12 mutants killed; exit 0, including cross-world shape history

verification.command: ssh <monitor-host> 'systemctl --user is-active explee-monitor.service; cd ~/explee-monitor && python3 spend_monitor.py stats'
verification.evidence: baseline service was active, but fresh verifier proved live source still predates the reviewed world-scoping fix; deploy and live parity check required

scope_changes.reason: The brief names alerts.jsonl as a deliverable of Task 1; it existed only on the collector host because publish.sh never sent it to the data branch, so both README links returned 404. Publishing it needs the alert log in the repository and the publishing script under review instead of host-only. PROBLEMS.md carries the stale entry this work closes.

User asked for the site to offer Russian alongside English (English stays the default) and for the agent trace to be delivered as a readable page rather than a raw log. The trace markdown stays the verbatim artefact; the page renders it without changing a word.
The trace page is generated from the verbatim markdown by a script, so the rendering is reproducible and auditable rather than hand-built HTML that could quietly differ from the artefact.
publish.sh is committed from Windows and executed on Linux; line endings must be decided by the repository, not by whichever machine commits.

User asked for one visual system across every published page and for the STT evidence page to be recomposed so models can be compared side by side. The STT pages are generated by explee-stt/render_evidence.py, so the change belongs in that generator; these paths are its output.

The rebuilt landing, dashboard and stand pages were authored in the session scratchpad and copied into docs/ byte-exact rather than retyped. The transfer guard requires a durable record for any copy, so the record itself has to be in scope.

The pages must be reviewed over http rather than file://, because a file:// origin cannot fetch data.json and renders as a dead snapshot. The launch entry serves docs/ with python -m http.server so the dashboard is checked with real data in both themes.

The trace now spans two harnesses and the page offers a disclosed spelling-corrected reading beside the verbatim default. Corrections are stored as explicit find/replace pairs so a reader can see exactly which characters changed; the verbatim file stays the artefact of record.

Exporting the review session found two defects in the exporter itself: a mid-turn prompt carrying an attachment arrives as a list of content blocks and crashed it, and harness notifications on that same path were labelled as messages the human typed, which is why the existing trace header counts 11 human messages where 10 is the truth.

The brief names alerts.jsonl as a deliverable and it was reachable only from the repository and the data branch, not from the site. A live viewer serves it from the same branch the collector publishes to, so the page cannot go stale the way a committed copy would.

The submission form takes six uploads and two links. The bundle is built from the repository's own files by a script so nothing in it is hand-assembled, and the checklist maps each form field to exactly one artefact.
